title: Films, Guide Lines, Gold Leaf, Depth & ASCII
description: A scroll that behaves like film stock, a probe that finds stray edges, grown drop caps, depth on a lock screen, UI in characters.

drops.title: The Scroll Is the Film
drops.description: Three beats on one pinned stage: layers parting, a route drawing itself, and a frame sequence scrubbed by the scrollbar.
drops.concept: Scrolltide's skill treats a scroll section as film: one pinned stage, one named scroll moment, and checkpoints at 0/25/50/75/100% to prove it never stalls. This rebuild runs all three of its headline patterns on one stage — six-layer parallax, a self-drawing SVG route with a travelling head, and a 48-frame strip generated in canvas and scrubbed frame by frame — with film length, parallax depth, beat easing and frame count all live.
drops.source: scrolltide/ai-studio-skill — scroll films, layered parallax, self-drawing paths

interaction.mouse: Scroll the page — the stage is pinned and every beat is driven by scroll offset.
interaction.click: Toggle the checkpoint rules, or rewind to frame 0.
interaction.touch: Swipe to scroll; the three progress segments track each beat.

drops.title: The Alignment Pass
drops.description: A probe measures every ink edge, clusters them into guide lines, and reports each item that misses by more than the threshold.
drops.concept: Gridlines runs an alignment pass over a rendered interface: draw the vertical guides, list every item whose leading edge misses one, fix the padding. Here the probe is real — it reads each element's box plus its own padding to find the ink edge, clusters the edges agglomeratively within the snap tolerance, puts each line on the modal edge so one stray cannot drag it, and then glides the offenders onto the line by animating their padding.
drops.source: pritamux/gridlines — an agent skill for alignment passes

interaction.mouse: Run the pass, then glide the strays onto their lines; drag the tolerance and threshold to change what counts as a miss.
interaction.click: Restore the sloppy padding to run the audit again from scratch.
interaction.touch: All controls are buttons and sliders; guides redraw on resize.

drops.title: Initials Grown, Not Picked
drops.description: Four illuminated drop caps drawn at view time — seeded frame, growing ornament, two misregistered inks and paper grain.
drops.concept: Initialis draws every ornamental initial in the browser when you look at it rather than serving a picture: a letter, a frame and ground, an ornament that grows, a texture and two or three inks on paper. This rebuild keeps that recipe in canvas — a seeded plan picks paper, inks, frame and corner motif, the vines grow out of the frame over time, and the letter prints twice with a small registration offset, Botanical, Gothic, Deco or Knot.
drops.source: azlen/initialis — endless explorer for ornamental drop caps

interaction.mouse: Click any initial to grow a new variation of that one; Wander reseeds all four.
interaction.click: More like this nudges every seed a little; density, saturation and growth time are live.
interaction.touch: Tap an initial to regrow it; type your own four letters.

drops.title: Slide to Unlock, With Depth
drops.description: Three lock screens whose subject stands in front of the clock, unlocked by dragging a knob through rubber-band resistance.
drops.concept: Camlo turns a still wallpaper into a depth-effect lock screen: the subject sits in front of the clock and the scene parts as the phone tilts, then the wallpaper morphs on unlock. Rebuilt on the web, each card layers sky, ridges, clock and subject at different depths, driven by pointer or by the gyroscope where it is allowed, and the unlock knob runs on a real spring with rubber-banding past the rail and a threshold that flips the scene to day.
drops.source: Kianuni/Camlo — depth and motion lock screens

interaction.mouse: Hover a card for parallax; drag the white knob to the right and release past the threshold.
interaction.click: Double-click a card to re-lock it; the panel tunes depth, stiffness, damping and threshold.
interaction.touch: Drag the knob with a finger; switch the tilt source to the gyroscope to part the layers by tilting.

drops.title: Components Drawn in ASCII
drops.description: A progress bar, a toggle, a sparkline and a button rendered as characters, with sharks swimming through them in four stages.
drops.concept: ascii-sharks draws its creatures as ASCII on a canvas, with drawing stages from spine to silhouette to shaded to full and an optional pointer interaction. This rebuild puts working UI into the same character grid: the components are real — the toggle flips, the button releases another shark, the progress bar resets on click — and the creatures are rasterised against a spine distance field, so the stage selector changes how much of each one is drawn.
drops.source: stackedlol/ascii-sharks — fish and sharks drawn as ASCII on a canvas

interaction.mouse: Move the pointer to push a wake through the characters and scare the sharks off course.
interaction.click: Click the toggle to flip currents, the button to release another shark, the bar to reset it.
interaction.touch: Tap the components; cell size, creature count and wake strength are sliders.
